claim: Indian nutraceutical/health supplement regulations (effective January 1 2018) require that individual nutrient content in health supplements must be at least 15% of ICMR RDA, and no supplement nutrient content may exceed the ICMR Recommended Daily Allowance.
stance_target: Regulatory ceilings and floors on nutrient content in Indian health supplements
scope_conditions: India; health supplements regulated under FSS (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals) Regulations 2016, effective January 1 2018
quoted_support: The amount of nutrients added to supplements can't go beyond the recommended daily allowance that has been set by Indian Council of Medical Research. When it comes to health supplements, the individual nutrient content can't be less than 15% of the recommended daily allowance. However, in case the claim is of higher nutrient content, it can't be less than 30% of the recommended daily allowance.
numbers: 30% of ICMR RDA (minimum for higher nutrient content claims)
entities: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India

claim: Indian food supplement regulations prohibit addition of hormones, steroids, and psychotropic drugs to health supplements and nutraceuticals.
stance_target: Indian regulatory prohibitions on supplement ingredients
quoted_support: hormones, steroids and psychotropic drugs can't be added to it.

claim: Indian supplement labeling must include 'Not for Medicinal Use' warning and a statement that the supplement cannot substitute for a regular diet.
stance_target: Mandatory labeling requirements for Indian nutraceuticals and health supplements
quoted_support: A warning- Not for Medicinal Use, should be written; Its content, purpose, and target age group; and A statement specifying that the supplement can't be used as a substitute for a regular diet.

claim: Nutraceuticals in India are classified under Category 13 (Foodstuffs for particular nutritional uses), specifically Category 13.6, and are not classified as drugs — this means CDSCO drug approval is not required but FSSAI compliance is mandatory.
stance_target: Regulatory classification of Vitamin D3 supplements in India as food/nutraceutical (FSSAI), not drug (CDSCO)
quoted_support: They are not medicinal products therefore its use is not expected to treat or prevent diseases in humans.
